candidates.name: Backward intertwiner across odometer fibers: two-ended opposite-drift weights making a fiber-moving backward shift a bounded element of {S}' (B16 weights, B17 drift lemma, B18 V)
candidates.statement: Over the 2-adic odometer theta, choose log-weights a_j(x) of a bilateral shift with quadratic growth and sub-leading corrections that increase by D at the positive end and decrease by D at the negative end when x -> theta x (except at a.e.-finitely many wraps). Then b~_j(x)=w_{j-1}(theta x)/(e^c w_j(x)) tends to 0 at both ends, sup_j b~_j(x)=L(x) is finite a.e., and V (Vf)(theta x)=V_x f(x), V_x e_j=(b~_j(x)/L(x)) e_{j-1} is a contraction commuting with S that maps each fiber tail K_{>=h} densely onto K_{>=h-1} of the next fiber.

neighbours.relation: unicellular weighted shifts -- the FIBERS, not the coupling

neighbours.ref: Atzmon-Sodin 1999; Atzmon's weighted l^2(Z) reformulation (in L / snippet)
neighbours.relation: single bilateral weighted shifts; a single fiber cannot carry a bounded backward intertwiner (w_{j-1}/w_j -> inf)
weighted translation operators decompose as direct integrals over ergodic transformations; no commutant/hyperinvariant analysis

neighbours.ref: Dykema 2005 Prop 2.1 + Haagerup-Schultz route (in L) and IP (same release)
neighbours.relation: commutant of T in a II_1 crossed product contains JMJ, i.e. symmetries that move along the base; IP uses this. BI's V is a hand-built decomposable analogue: a single commuting operator that moves fibers and tails at once.
density for transitive algebras containing a MASA / finite-multiplicity abelian algebra; BI lives in the infinite-multiplicity gap
neighbours.verdict: problem-level boundary, not a precedent for the device

neighbours.ref: Ergodic cocycle theory: coboundaries with non-integrable, a.e.-finite transfer functions (classical; e.g. IP's own coboundary step)
neighbours.relation: pattern of exploiting pointwise-finite but non-integrable constants (C(x), L(x))
counterexamples on l^1 / Banach spaces by entirely different (combinatorial-analytic) constructions; no Hilbert-space analogue

The intertwiner branch (ExplicitWeights, BackwardWeights, HaarBase, GlobalOperators, FiberMaps) is ~0.94k of ~2.5k direct-route DAG lines (~37%); the core (excluding Domar re-proof and plumbing) is essentially E1 + the 0.2k transitivity file.

test4.pivot_distance: estimated 2 from L- : (i) decide on a decomposable model (fibers unicellular, base ergodic) whose commutant contains a fiber-moving element -- suggested by the II_1 route but not stated in L; (ii) write the commutation recurrence (forced) and design weights with opposite drift at the two ends so the solution is bounded. final.F: F3 (auxiliary construction), with F5 flavour (one translation group spread over an ergodic base so that its inverse becomes bounded)
final.justification: No source in any searched field contains a bounded commuting operator that moves invariant tails backward between fibers of an ergodic base; single-fiber versions are impossible (unbounded), and the known II_1 route reaches the HSP only via the far heavier IP machinery. The device is tiny and invisible in the goal, and if correct it resolves a ~50-year-old problem in ~10 pages. Downgrade risks: (a) pivot is short once the II_1 commutant analogy is in mind (the same release produced IP first or simultaneously); (b) an expert may recognize the opposite-drift cocycle trick from ergodic theory or from older operator-theory folklore; (c) correctness rests on Lean compilation; (d) contamination: IP is same-day model output that already points to transitive commutants via base dynamics.

candidates.name: Conditional convolution obstruction with endpoint-conditioned tail attenuation on ordered biased couplings (C15-C17)
candidates.statement: If all products A_v B_{-n-v} sum to zero, the finite-window coefficients are bounded below on an event of probability c, and each tail ratio is bounded by eta plus indicators of events with conditional probability <= delta given x (resp. y), then c eps <= (2K+1)(eta + 2 sqrt(delta)).

neighbours.relation: existence of couplings with prescribed marginals; IP notes the order relation is not closed so Edwards Cor 3.2 does not apply directly

neighbours.ref: Titchmarsh convolution theorem; Domar 1981/1983 support theorems (Domar in L)

neighbours.relation: bounding sum_v |xi_v(x) gamma_{n+v}(y)| 1_{H} by conditioning one factor on each endpoint

family_D.rests_on: E1 alone (backward intertwiner with two-ended opposite drift over the odometer). The IP machinery (E2-E4) is N2.
family_D.falls_to: D2 if (a) the test-4 L- arm finds the device at a rate above the calibrated threshold (risk: once 'decomposable model with fiber-moving commutant element' is suggested, the recurrence is forced); (b) an expert identifies an earlier fibred-shift or opposite-drift construction in operator theory or ergodic theory; (c) the Lean comparators fail to compile (then the claim itself is in doubt).
family_D.not_transfer: Domar unicellularity (harmonic analysis), the odometer and recurrence (ergodic theory), direct integrals and the II_1 route are transfer/N0. The candidate is the specific coupling of fibers by a bounded commuting backward shift; no precedent for it was found.
family_D.correctness_caveat: Grades are conditional on correctness of an extraordinary claim (negative HSP and transitive algebra problem). The BI proof is short and I found no gap; the Lean proves the comparator statement twice (BI direct; IP product model) with a clean text-level trust surface (two run_cmd environment edits, empty definition_names to check). Conflicts with Garayev 2026 and Lee 2023 (affirmative claims, preprints) and Cho-Ko-Lee 2017 Cor 2.8 (published).
family_D.compression_note: No step-3b run. BI vs IP is a natural compression comparison: the same HSP conclusion costs ~2.5k Lean lines via E1 vs ~15k (product model) / ~28k (circle model) via the II_1 route -- a 6-11x drop attributable mainly to E1 (plus unicellular fibers).
